initial.title: [v0.92.1][DEC-01] Runtime v2/v3 authority separation
initial.goal: Produce one independently owned Runtime v2 and Runtime v3 authority topology with executable migration and rollback proof while excluding Runtime v4.
initial.required_outcome: One accepted Runtime v2/v3 source and authority topology, backed by executable source-denominator, reverse-reference, compatibility, rollback, and migration checks.
authority_boundary: Runtime v2 authority remains under adl/src/runtime_v2/**.
Runtime v3 authority remains under adl-runtime/** and adl-runtime-kernel/**.
Shared docs and DEC-01 evidence record topology and proof only; they do not move runtime authority silently.
Runtime v4 is excluded and any v4 requirement stops the issue for replanning.
Issue #513 does not absorb #483 or sibling Sprint 1 work.
operator_constraints: Use the canonical FastWork issue worktree.
Use typed C-SDLC v2 routes only for lifecycle writes.
Publish with Closes #513 and keep CI green before merge.
initial.task_boundary: Exactly one accepted Runtime v2/v3 authority topology with executable migration and rollback checks; no Runtime v4 work and no sibling Sprint 1 scope.
deliverables: Executable validator covering source denominator, reverse-reference census, compatibility, rollback, migration, and Runtime v4 exclusion.
Fresh independent exact-head review and green PR closing #513.
acceptance_criteria: AC-1: Every declared Runtime v2 and Runtime v3 source root exists and has one owner and disposition.
AC-2: Current reverse references to Runtime v2 and Runtime v3 are inventoried with one owner/disposition.
AC-3: Supported behavior has an executable compatibility proof.
AC-4: Rollback and migration are executable dry-run contracts.
AC-5: Runtime v4 remains excluded from source ownership, migration, and rollback authority.
initial.plan_summary: Bind #513 in FastWork, add a runtime authority topology document, machine-readable manifest, and executable validator, run focused proof, obtain fresh exact-head review, publish, shepherd green checks, and merge through typed C-SDLC v2.

steps.action: Bind #513 and establish issue-local lifecycle state.
Author the Runtime v2/v3 authority topology and manifest.
Implement executable validation for denominator, reverse references, compatibility, rollback, migration, and Runtime v4 exclusion.
Run focused validation and finalize implemented truth.
Obtain fresh exact-head review, publish, shepherd, merge, and finish.

invariants: Every source root has exactly one declared owner.
Reverse references are either owned, compatibility-only, documentation-only, or evidence-only.
Migration and rollback are explicit dry-run contracts.
Runtime v4 does not appear as a source owner or migration target.
risks: Reverse-reference census can drift as sibling PRs land.
A documentation-only topology could overclaim behavior if not backed by executable checks.
Runtime v4 mentions in historical planning docs could be mistaken for current authority.
Source ownership could become ambiguous if Runtime v2 imports Runtime v3 or vice versa.
stop_conditions: Either runtime silently acquires the other runtime's authority.
The issue branch or worktree identity drifts.
Fresh review finds unresolved actionable issues.

validation_lanes.proof_role: Validate DEC-01 source ownership, reverse-reference dispositions, compatibility command, migration dry-run, rollback dry-run, and Runtime v4 exclusion.
Validate whitespace hygiene for tracked DEC-01 changes.

initial.failure_policy: Fail closed on unowned source roots, unclassified reverse references, missing compatibility proof, non-executable migration or rollback dry-run, Runtime v4 authority expansion, stale review, red CI, or lifecycle topology drift.
review_prompts: Does the manifest assign every declared Runtime v2/v3 source root one owner and disposition?
Does the reverse-reference census cover the current repo references without leaving supported consumers unclassified?
Are migration and rollback executable dry-run contracts rather than prose-only claims?
Does the implementation avoid Runtime v4 scope and sibling Sprint 1 work?
Are the validation lanes sufficient for DEC-01's bounded authority-separation result?
initial.review_scope: Issue #513 DEC-01 changed docs, evidence, validation script, lifecycle state, and exact branch revision.
